prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Everything is verified and uSync captured the schema. Here's the final report.

---

## What I built

A two-post blog site demonstrating the Umbraco MCP server end to end, built entirely with blocks and the block grid, following the prescribed order: **model → content → rebuild → Razor**.

**Content model (all via MCP, no migrations):**
- **Page types** — `blogFrontPage`, `blogPost` (with Title/Intro/Blocks and Summary/CoverImage/PublishedDate/Blocks), each with a template. The front page got the `/` domain.
- **5 block element types** — `heroBlock`, `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`, `callToActionBlock`.
- **1 composition** — `blockSettings` (anchor + "Block Spacing" dropdown) composed onto every block, so anchor/spacing are content-level block properties.
- **Data types** — a Block Spacing dropdown and a Block Grid; all filed under the scaffold's six folders.
- **Content** — front page (hero → richtext → CTA) and two published posts ("Why MCP Is Awesome: Plumbing…" and "MCP as a Network: Every Tool a Node", each hero → richtext → image → quote → CTA, with external CTA links to modelcontextprotocol.io). All 10 Unsplash photos imported into a `Blog` media folder and used via MediaPicker3.

**Razor (Umbraco's own rendering pipeline, no custom renderers):**
- Templates render blocks with `@await Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks")`; the front page lists published posts via `Model.Children<BlogPost>()` with signed `GetCropUrl()` crops.
- 5 adapter partials at `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml` → 5 ViewComponents (`Hero`, `RichText`, `Image`, `Quote`, `CallToAction`), plain models in `Models/Blocks/`, markup in `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` (Tailwind).
- Added the (missing) `umb-block-grid` layout CSS + rich-text typography to the Frontend Tailwind bundle and built it into `wwwroot/dist`.

## How to view

Site is running on **https://localhost:44317** (started via `dotnet run`):
- Front page: `/` (hero, intro richtext, CTA, and a "Latest posts" card grid)
- Post 1: `/mcp-as-a-network-every-tool-a-node/`
- Post 2: `/why-mcp-is-awesome-plumbing-that-connects-the-stack/`
- Backoffice at `/umbraco` shows the whole tree/model. uSync exported everything to `uSync/v18/`.

Verified: all three pages HTTP 200, block counts 3 / 5 / 5, rich text renders as real HTML, signed image crops resolve, zero render exceptions in the logs.

## Anything not working / notes

- **Block Grid validation gotcha** — the Block Grid data type enforced its `validationLimit` literally (`max: 0` = zero blocks allowed) and every publish failed until I set the limits to `null`. Fixed via MCP before publishing.
- **Rich text double-encoding** — in v18 `IHtmlEncodedString` is *not* `IHtmlContent`, so `@Model.BodyText` emits escaped markup. Fixed by restoring the raw string with `ToHtmlString()` and rendering via `@Html.Raw` in the component view.
- **Grid styleship** — Umbraco ships the block-grid markup but no stylesheet, so I added the `.umb-block-grid` layout rules to the Frontend `site.css` (the local `Views/Partials/blockgrid/*` partials are untouched, per the rules).
- **Minor** — the front page's `intro` property currently serves as the page's meta description; the visible intro lives in the hero block. The pre-existing `SixLabors.ImageSharp` NuGet vulnerability warnings come from the scaffold's locked deps, not this work.
